name: RBI Grade B
fullName: Reserve Bank of India – Officers in Grade 'B' (DR) General: Phase I
eligibility: Graduate with ≥60% (55% for SC/ST/PwBD) or post-graduate with ≥55% (pass for SC/ST/PwBD); 21–30 years (relaxations apply); limited number of attempts for the General stream

notification.summary: The 2026 cycle (≈60 posts: ≈40 General, ≈10 DEPR, ≈10 DSIM as reported) is in its final stage: Phase I for the General stream was held on 13 Jun 2026 and Phase II on 25 Jul 2026; the Phase II result/interview shortlist was reported in Aug 2026 and the final result was awaited in late Sep 2026. The next notification is expected around Apr–May 2027. Dates are from education portals; the RBI site could not be opened from the research environment.

pattern.notes: Sectional timing (approx.): GA 25 min, Reasoning 45 min, English 25 min, Quant 25 min. Sectional and aggregate cut-offs apply; Phase I is qualifying only. Phase II has three papers (Economic & Social Issues, English writing, Finance & Management) followed by an interview (Phase II + interview decide the merit).

trendAnalysis.summary: Phase I is moderate overall; reasoning (puzzles of 5–6 sets: square/circular tables, box, floor, year/age-based) is the most time-consuming and was rated moderate-to-difficult in 2026. GA carries 80 marks and is dominated by 6–8 months of current affairs on banking, RBI policy, economy, government schemes, international reports and appointments; static questions are few. Quant is DI-heavy (missing-data tables, caselets) and in 2026 swapped quadratic equations for simplification/approximation. English (RC, cloze, error spotting, fillers, para-jumbles) was easier than 2025. Overall good attempts were reported around 100–115 with cut-offs near 100 ± 5.

topics.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)

resources.notes: RBI does not publish Phase I objective papers or answer keys; candidates receive their marks after each phase. Notifications, syllabus and results are on opportunities.rbi.org.in (Current Vacancies / Results). Previous papers in circulation are memory-based compilations by coaching institutes; RBI publications (Annual Report, Monetary Policy Statements, Financial Stability Report) are the main official sources for GA and Phase II.

questions.question: Under which section of the RBI Act, 1934 is the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) constituted?
questions.explanation: Section 45ZB provides for the constitution of the MPC; Section 45ZA deals with the inflation target.

questions.question: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework that came into effect in 2016, the CPI inflation target set for the RBI was:
questions.explanation: The target was 4% CPI inflation with an upper tolerance of 6% and a lower tolerance of 2%.

questions.question: How many members does the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee have, and who has the casting vote in case of a tie?
options: Six; the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy
questions.explanation: The MPC has six members (three from RBI, three external); the Governor has a casting vote in a tie.

questions.question: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF), introduced by the RBI in April 2022, functions as:
options: The floor of the LAF corridor
The ceiling of the LAF corridor
questions.explanation: SDF, a collateral-free liquidity absorption tool, replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the LAF corridor; the MSF is the ceiling.

questions.question: Scheduled banks maintain the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) under which provision?
options: Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
questions.explanation: CRR is prescribed under Section 42 of the RBI Act, 1934; SLR is under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.question: A term loan is classified as a Non-Performing Asset when interest or instalment of principal remains overdue for more than:
questions.explanation: Under RBI's IRAC norms, a loan becomes an NPA when interest/principal is overdue for more than 90 days.

questions.question: The SARFAESI Act, which lets secured creditors enforce security without court intervention, was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act was enacted in 2002.

questions.question: For domestic scheduled commercial banks, the overall priority sector lending target is:
options: 40% of ANBC or CEOE, whichever is higher
questions.explanation: The overall PSL target is 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure, whichever is higher (18% is the agriculture sub-target).

questions.question: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of:
questions.explanation: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI.

questions.question: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was developed by:
questions.explanation: UPI was developed and is operated by NPCI; it was launched in 2016.

questions.question: Who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (as of 2026)?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Malhotra took charge as the 26th Governor of the RBI in December 2024.

questions.question: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: BIS, often called the central bank of central banks, is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

questions.question: The 'World Economic Outlook' report is published by:
questions.explanation: The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook, usually in April and October.

questions.question: NABARD was established in which year?
questions.explanation: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the CRAFICARD (Shivaraman) committee.

questions.question: The issued capital of a Regional Rural Bank is shared by the Central Government, the State Government and the sponsor bank in the ratio:
questions.explanation: Central Government 50%, State Government 15% and sponsor bank 35%.

questions.question: Who chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission, whose award covers 2026-27 to 2030-31?
questions.explanation: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted in December 2023 under Dr Arvind Panagariya.

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: The GST Council is a constitutional body under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Amendment, 2016) provides for the GST Council. Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission.

questions.question: Under the RBI's Scale-Based Regulation framework for NBFCs, how many layers are NBFCs placed in?
questions.explanation: Four layers: Base, Middle, Upper and Top (the Top layer is ideally expected to remain empty).

questions.question: Under the RBI's revised Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework for banks (effective 2022), which areas are monitored?
questions.explanation: The revised PCA tracks capital, asset quality (net NPA) and leverage; profitability (return on assets) was dropped as a trigger.

questions.question: The RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, which follows a 'One Nation One Ombudsman' approach, was launched in:
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 was launched in November 2021.

questions.question: To curb digital fraud, the RBI directed banks to migrate their websites to which exclusive internet domain?
questions.explanation: Banks were asked to shift to the exclusive '.bank.in' domain (registered through IDRBT); '.fin.in' was proposed for other financial entities.

questions.question: In its June 2025 policy, the RBI announced a phased cut in the Cash Reserve Ratio to:
questions.explanation: The CRR was cut by 100 basis points, from 4% to 3% of NDTL, in four equal tranches during Sep–Nov 2025.

questions.question: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961, comes into force from:
questions.explanation: The new Income-tax Act, 2025 takes effect from 1 April 2026 (tax year 2026-27).

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: Under the GST rate rationalisation effective 22 September 2025, the two main GST slabs are:
questions.explanation: The four-slab structure was replaced by two main slabs of 5% and 18%, with a special 40% rate for select luxury and sin goods.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit around a square table. Four sit at the four corners facing the centre and four sit at the middle of the four sides facing away from the centre. J sits at a corner. Q sits third to the left of J. N sits opposite J. M sits immediately to the right of J. K is an immediate neighbour of N and faces away from the centre. O faces away from the centre. L is not an immediate neighbour of M. Only one person sits between N and P.

Who sits second to the right of K?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from J (corner): J, O, L, Q, N, K, P, M. Corner-sitters face the centre (right = anticlockwise); side-sitters face outward (right = clockwise). K faces outward, so second to its right (clockwise) is M.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit around a square table. Four sit at the four corners facing the centre and four sit at the middle of the four sides facing away from the centre. J sits at a corner. Q sits third to the left of J. N sits opposite J. M sits immediately to the right of J. K is an immediate neighbour of N and faces away from the centre. O faces away from the centre. L is not an immediate neighbour of M. Only one person sits between N and P.

Who sits immediately to the left of L?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: J, O, L, Q, N, K, P, M. L sits at a corner facing the centre, so his left is clockwise — Q.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit around a square table. Four sit at the four corners facing the centre and four sit at the middle of the four sides facing away from the centre. J sits at a corner. Q sits third to the left of J. N sits opposite J. M sits immediately to the right of J. K is an immediate neighbour of N and faces away from the centre. O faces away from the centre. L is not an immediate neighbour of M. Only one person sits between N and P.

Which group consists only of persons who face away from the centre?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: J (corner), O, L (corner), Q, N (corner), K, P (corner), M. The side-sitters O, Q, K and M face away from the centre.

questions.question:
Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G were born in different years among 1971, 1978, 1985, 1990, 1996, 2001 and 2008. Ages are calculated as on the same date in 2026 (age = 2026 − birth year). The sum of the ages of C and B is 73, and C is older than B. D was born in an even-numbered year, after G. A is 11 years older than D. Only one person was born between G and E (in order of birth years). F is younger than G. G was born in a year that is a multiple of 5.

What is G's age in 2026?

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G were born in different years among 1971, 1978, 1985, 1990, 1996, 2001 and 2008. Ages are calculated as on the same date in 2026 (age = 2026 − birth year). The sum of the ages of C and B is 73, and C is older than B. D was born in an even-numbered year, after G. A is 11 years older than D. Only one person was born between G and E (in order of birth years). F is younger than G. G was born in a year that is a multiple of 5.

Who was born in 1978?
questions.explanation: C + B = 73 with C older gives C–B = 55–18 or 48–25. A − D = 11 needs (41, 30) or (36, 25). D even and after G, G a multiple of 5, F after G, one person between G and E: only C 1971, E 1978, A 1985, G 1990, D 1996, F 2001, B 2008 works. E was born in 1978.

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G were born in different years among 1971, 1978, 1985, 1990, 1996, 2001 and 2008. Ages are calculated as on the same date in 2026 (age = 2026 − birth year). The sum of the ages of C and B is 73, and C is older than B. D was born in an even-numbered year, after G. A is 11 years older than D. Only one person was born between G and E (in order of birth years). F is younger than G. G was born in a year that is a multiple of 5.

What is the sum of the ages of A and F in 2026?

Eight boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 8 the top). Only three boxes are kept between P and T. T is kept at one of the two lowest positions. The number of boxes above V is equal to the number of boxes below P. Q is kept immediately below V. R is kept somewhere above U, and only one box is kept between R and S. W is kept adjacent to Q.

Which box is kept at the top?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: T, W, Q, V, P, S, U, R. R is at the top.

questions.question:
Eight boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 8 the top). Only three boxes are kept between P and T. T is kept at one of the two lowest positions. The number of boxes above V is equal to the number of boxes below P. Q is kept immediately below V. R is kept somewhere above U, and only one box is kept between R and S. W is kept adjacent to Q.

How many boxes are kept between W and U?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: T, W, Q, V, P, S, U, R. Between W (2) and U (7) are Q, V, P and S — four.

questions.question:
Eight boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 8 the top). Only three boxes are kept between P and T. T is kept at one of the two lowest positions. The number of boxes above V is equal to the number of boxes below P. Q is kept immediately below V. R is kept somewhere above U, and only one box is kept between R and S. W is kept adjacent to Q.

Which box is kept immediately above P?
questions.explanation: If T = 1, P = 5; boxes above V = boxes below P = 4, so V = 4 and Q = 3; W adjacent to Q is 2. R above U with one box between R and S gives S = 6, U = 7, R = 8. (T = 2 leads to a contradiction.) S is immediately above P.

questions.question:
Statements: Only a few banks are lenders. All lenders are institutions. No institution is a broker.
Conclusions: I. Some banks are not brokers. II. Some brokers are lenders.
questions.explanation: Banks that are lenders are institutions and hence not brokers — I follows. No lender (an institution) can be a broker — II is false.

questions.question:
Statements: All coins are notes. Some notes are cheques. No cheque is a draft.
Conclusions: I. Some coins being drafts is a possibility. II. No note is a draft.
questions.explanation: Coins are notes, and notes that are not cheques may be drafts, so coins being drafts is possible — I follows. Some notes may be drafts, so II is not definite.

questions.question:
Statements: P ≥ Q > R ≤ S; T > Q ≥ U
Conclusions: I. T > R  II. P ≥ U
questions.explanation: T > Q > R gives T > R; P ≥ Q ≥ U gives P ≥ U. Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: A ≤ B < C = D; E > D ≥ F; G ≥ E
Conclusions: I. G > B  II. F < C
questions.explanation: G ≥ E > D = C > B gives G > B. F ≤ D = C gives only F ≤ C, so 'F < C' is not definite. Only I follows.

questions.question: In a family, L is the mother of M. M is married to N. O is the son of N. P is the sister of O. Q is the father of N. R is the wife of Q. How is R related to P?
questions.explanation: N is the child of Q and R. O and P are N's children. So R is P's grandmother.

questions.question: Point A is 12 m east of point B. Point C is 5 m north of A. Point D is 4 m west of C. Point E is 11 m south of D. How far and in which direction is E from B?
questions.explanation: Take B = (0,0): A = (12,0), C = (12,5), D = (8,5), E = (8,−6). Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m, towards the South-East.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'policy rate cut' is written as 'mi ka lo', 'rate hike likely' as 'zo lo pa' and 'cut likely soon' as 'pa mi ru'. What is the code for 'policy'?
questions.explanation: rate = lo (1 & 2), cut = mi (1 & 3), likely = pa (2 & 3). The remaining code in sentence 1, ka, means 'policy'.

questions.question:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row of six seats facing north. Who sits at the extreme right end?
I. A sits third from the left end. B sits second to the right of A.
II. C sits immediately to the right of B.
options: The data in statement I alone are sufficient, but the data in statement II alone are not
The data in statement II alone are sufficient, but the data in statement I alone are not
The data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are necessary
questions.explanation: I alone gives A = 3, B = 5 but not who is at seat 6. II alone gives no seat numbers. Together, C = 6 — so both are needed.

questions.question:
Statement: An advertisement says, 'Use our UPI app — zero charges on all transfers.'
Assumptions: I. People prefer not to pay charges on money transfers. II. No other app offers zero-charge transfers.
options: Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: The advertisement assumes zero charges will attract users (I is implicit). It does not assume that no competitor offers the same (II is not implicit).

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

When a central bank raises interest rates, the effect on inflation is neither immediate nor uniform. Higher policy rates first feed into money-market rates and bond yields; bank lending rates adjust more slowly, depending on how loans are benchmarked and how much competition banks face for deposits. Households may postpone purchases of cars and homes, and firms may defer investment, but these decisions unfold over several quarters. Meanwhile, supply shocks — a failed harvest or a spike in global oil prices — can push prices up regardless of monetary policy. This is why most central banks target inflation over a medium-term horizon and try to anchor expectations through clear communication. If people believe the central bank will act to bring inflation back to target, they are less likely to demand large wage increases or raise prices pre-emptively, which itself makes the central bank's task easier.

According to the passage, what adjusts first after a central bank raises its policy rate?
questions.explanation: 'Higher policy rates first feed into money-market rates and bond yields; bank lending rates adjust more slowly.'

Because governments require it by law

Because bond yields never respond to policy rates

questions.question:
Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The government's decision to ______ the import duty on edible oils is expected to bring relief to consumers.
questions.explanation: Only a reduction in duty lowers prices and brings relief to consumers.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
Not only the employees (A)/ but also the manager were (B)/ surprised by the sudden (C)/ announcement of the merger. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation: With 'not only … but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'the manager' (singular): 'was surprised'. Error in part B.

questions.question:
Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The minister's speech was so ______ that the audience lost interest within minutes.
questions.explanation: Losing interest within minutes implies the speech was tedious (boring); the others mean the opposite.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
A. Such tools, however, also raise questions about data privacy.
B. Banks are increasingly using artificial intelligence to assess loan applications.
C. Regulators are therefore drafting guidelines on how customer data may be used.
D. These systems can analyse thousands of data points in seconds.
E. This speeds up approvals and can reduce human bias.
questions.explanation: B (AI in lending) → D (capability) → E (benefit) → A ('however', privacy concern) → C ('therefore', regulation): BDEAC.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to bite the bullet'.
options: To face a difficult situation with courage
questions.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept and face something unpleasant or difficult bravely.

questions.question:
The table shows the revenue (₹ crore) of five companies in 2025 and their expenditure as a percentage of revenue. Profit = Revenue − Expenditure.
Company | Revenue | Expenditure (% of revenue)
P | 250 | 80%
Q | 320 | 75%
R | 400 | 85%
S | 180 | 70%
T | 300 | 90%

Which company earned the highest profit?
questions.explanation: Profits: P 50, Q 80, R 60, S 54, T 30 (₹ crore). Q is highest.

questions.explanation: Revenue = 400 × 1.15 = 460; expenditure = 340 × 1.10 = 374. Profit = 460 − 374 = ₹86 crore.

questions.question:
Solve and compare.
I. x² − 2x − 15 = 0
II. y² + 8y + 15 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation: I: (x − 5)(x + 3) = 0 → x = 5, −3. II: (y + 3)(y + 5) = 0 → y = −3, −5. Every x is greater than or equal to every y (−3 = −3), so x ≥ y.

(19.97)² − 14.02 × 11.98 + 3.98³ ≈ ?
Find the next term: 4, 5, 14, 39, 88, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are 1², 3², 5², 7²; next 9² = 81: 88 + 81 = 169.

questions.question: ₹20,000 is invested partly at 8% and partly at 12% simple interest per annum. If the total interest after one year is ₹2,000, how much was invested at 12%?
A, B and C can finish a job in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. All three start together, but A leaves after 2 days. In how many days in total is the job completed?
questions.explanation: Per day (in 60ths): A 6, B 5, C 4. First 2 days: 2 × 15 = 30/60. Remaining 30/60 at 9/60 per day = 10/3 days. Total = 2 + 3⅓ = 5⅓ days.
